newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON PRAISES UNITED, SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WRIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON PRAISES UNITED, SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WRIGHT.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson said he was delighted with his team's battling 2-1 win over Arsenal in the English premier league on Wednesday, describing their top-of-the-table victory as "extremely significant".
"This game had to be won tonight," he said. "Arsenal is never an easy place to come to and they have had a terrific season. It was an important victory and a very significnt one."

The win, courtesy of first half goals from Andy Cole and Ole Solskjaer, kept the champions at the top of the table, a point clear of Liverpool and five ahead of third-placed Arsenal, who have played a match more than United.

But Ferguson refused to be drawn on what appeared to be an outrageous Ian Wright foul on United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel after 76 minutes. Wright launched himself into a flying two-footed tackle on the Dane.
"Every time I come to London I get misquoted," Ferguson said, "so I am going to keep my thoughts in my big Scottish head. I have nothing to say about it."
The two players were also involved in an scuffle at the entrance to the players' tunnel after the match, but Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger attempted to play down the incident.

"The referee on the field had to be the judge of what happened and he and the linesman were in the best position to see the incident. Every time Ian Wright is involved in anything it becomes a major issue with the whole country talking about it. I don't know if anything happened in the tunnel, I can't speak about that."
Wright had earlier been booked for a scything tackle on Denis Irwin and was then frustrated by having a goal disallowed for offside after 68 minutes.
But a few minutes later, after being flagged offside, he chased a loose ball through to Schmeichel and appeared to lunge at him with both feet.

Ferguson reacted angrily and had to be restrained from going on to the pitch by two stewards. Afterwards Wenger said: "I thought (Ferguson's) reaction was suprising. After all, you can only have 11 men on the field."
While he was lucky to stay on the field, Wright will be suspended for two matches for the booking.
The two goals capped a magnificent opening 45 minutes for United in a match which only went ahead after a pitch inspection following a deluge just before the kickoff.
But while United swamped Arsenal in the first half, they had to hang on doggedly for the points after Dennis Bergkamp scored for Arsenal with 21 minutes to go.
United have now lost only once in their last six visits to Highbury and became the first team to beat Arsenal at home in the league this season.

As Wenger said afterwards: "This was a very, very important match for us to win. Mathematically it is not over and it depends on how we react against Wimbledon on Sunday but they are a very good team."
More bad news for the Gunners came when it was revealed Wright, Steve Bould and Ray Parlour would all be suspended following their bookings.
"That is very bad for us. I'll have to go out and buy some new players tonight," Wenger joked.
United's second-half substitute Nicky Butt injured an ankle and is likely to miss their European Cup quarter-final first leg against Porto in two weeks time.
